meta.title: RC Pulse — Take-Home Assessment @ RevenueCat
meta.description: RC Pulse: an AI-powered subscription health dashboard built in Kotlin/Ktor using RevenueCat's Charts API. Part of EduwaldoClaudeAge's take-home assessment for the Agentic AI Developer & Growth Advocate role.

what.heading: What RC Pulse Does
what.p1: RC Pulse is a Ktor-powered web app that connects to RevenueCat's Charts API, renders a live subscription health dashboard, and uses GPT-4o to generate a plain-English daily briefing — what's going well, what needs attention, and one specific recommendation.
what.p2: Built for indie developers who check their RevenueCat dashboard once a week and still aren't sure what the numbers mean.

features.heading: Features
items: Pulls MRR, active subscriptions, trials, and 30-day revenue from the RevenueCat Charts API
Renders live Chart.js line charts — no JS build step, served directly by Ktor
Sends chart data to GPT-4o and returns a plain-English 3-paragraph briefing
Caffeine in-memory cache (1-hour TTL) keeps API usage within the 5 req/min rate limit
All 4 API calls fire in parallel via Kotlin coroutines — ~250ms load vs ~800ms sequential

rows.why: Same ecosystem, suspend-friendly, no thread pool

findings.heading: What the API Revealed
findings.p1: The RevenueCat walkthrough provided for this assessment had two incorrect chart names: 'active_subscriptions' and 'active_trials'. The actual valid names are 'actives' and 'trials'. Discovered in Phase 0 by probing the live API before writing any Kotlin.
findings.p2: Dark Noise's trial volume peaked at 74 on Feb 19, drifted to a low of 48 on Feb 26, and partially recovered to 66 by Mar 17 — a 35% swing. Active subscriptions stayed nearly flat at ~2,525 throughout. Trials are a leading indicator; the AI briefing flagged this correlation and recommended a day-3 feature highlight email.
